title: UVM: Build an Agent (Active/Passive)
constraints: Write `class bus_agent extends uvm_agent`. In `build_phase`, read `is_active` from `uvm_config_db#(uvm_active_passive_enum)` with field name `"is_active"` (leave the inherited default, `UVM_ACTIVE`, if nothing was set).
Always build `mon` (a `bus_monitor`). Only build `drv` (a `bus_driver`) and `sqr` (a `uvm_sequencer #(bus_item)`) when `get_is_active() == UVM_ACTIVE`.
In `connect_phase`, connect `drv.seq_item_port` to `sqr.seq_item_export` — again, only when active.

`bus_driver` and `bus_monitor` are already fully implemented (see below); you are only writing the agent that assembles them. The UVM library is the Verilator-compatible chipsalliance/uvm-verilator (UVM 2017), and building it takes about a minute.
hints: `uvm_active_passive_enum` and the `is_active` field already exist on `uvm_agent` — you don't declare them yourself, just call `get_is_active()` after setting them.

`uvm_config_db#(uvm_active_passive_enum)::get(this, "", "is_active", is_active)` returns 0 (and leaves `is_active` untouched) when nothing was configured, so a bare `void'(...)` call is enough — you don't need to branch on the return value.
A passive agent's monitor still needs its virtual interface: build it exactly the same way as the active case, just without the driver/sequencer.

examples.check: active agent: driver drives items and the monitor observes all of them
examples.title: active agent

examples.check: passive agent: monitor still observes externally-driven bus activity
examples.title: passive agent
examples.input: 15 transfers driven directly on the bus (no sequencer)
